stories.title: Scientists redetermine a key strontium frequency with 50 times better precision for quantum technologies
stories.desc: The Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS) has remeasured a key transition frequency of the strontium (Sr) atom for the first time in 88 years, since 1938, using a photonic grating chip. It has established a new absolute frequency value with a measurement uncertainty reduced by…

stories.title: Forgotten particle could answer mystery of why we exist, say physicists
stories.desc: Scientists have unveiled a new theory on the birth of the cosmos, suggesting the early universe was shaped by an ancient particle that has been overlooked for decades.

stories.title: Auroral Structure Could Be Caused by Bouncing Electrons
stories.desc: High-resolution optical observations of aurorae show fluctuations and structuring that could be explained by interactions between electrons and a plasma phenomenon called Alfvén waves.

stories.title: Sentinel-3C captures Hurricane Rachel
stories.desc: Image: Demonstrating that the visible channels of Sentinel-3C’s sea and land surface temperature radiometer are working as expected, on 2 October the instrument captured this image of Hurricane Rachel over the eastern Pacific Ocean, off the coast of Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula.

stories.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
stories.desc: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this one has been unpacked by human experts. The implications, one mathematician said, are “staggering.” The post AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now? first appeared on Quanta Magazine

stories.title: Equatorial Pacific Warming Pattern Mitigated by Slow Ocean Adjustment
stories.desc: Model simulations under an abrupt 4x CO 2 scenario reveal that initially enhanced gradients in sea surface temperature under global warming are then mitigated by circulation changes.

stories.title: Biosignatures Extend Robustly into the Top Kilometer of Sedimentary Basins
stories.desc: Through the top kilometer of sedimentary basins, biosignatures track microbial cells, permeability, and water inputs. Below that, permeability limits microbial presence despite temperatures conducive to life.
